content:
CCTV footage surfaced on social media today (the 17th), showing a clip that appears to be from a back alley. Three people are seen chatting, and at least two are clearly visible wearing uniforms of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD). Based on the FEHD uniform information, the two are suspected to be a Hawker Control Officer and a Senior Hawker Control Officer.

The clip shows two officer-level personnel chatting in the back alley. One first took out a cigarette and smoked it, then another senior hawker control officer walked over, took out a cigarette pack and a lighter, brushed back their hair, placed a cigarette in their mouth, and when walking away from the camera with their back turned, a wisp of smoke was seen emanating from their side.

The Collective (集誌社) inquired with the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department whether the individuals in the footage are FEHD staff. The department confirmed in response to the inquiry that the individuals in the footage are members of the FEHD's district hawker control team. The spokesperson stated that the incident occurred in early June this year. The reporter asked whether FEHD personnel are permitted to smoke while wearing their uniforms. If the footage is genuine, have the personnel violated any rules? Will it affect the department's image? The FEHD replied that according to the department's established regulations, personnel are prohibited from smoking while wearing their uniforms and in public places.

The FEHD stated that the department places great emphasis on employee discipline and professional conduct, and has initiated a disciplinary investigation into the incident. Appropriate action will be taken in accordance with established procedures and the investigation results. The spokesperson also added that the department has clear requirements regarding the conduct of personnel while wearing their uniforms, and any behavior that violates the department's disciplinary requirements will be followed up on strictly.
